messages.content: "In a game of basketball, a player has a 60% chance of making a successful shot. In a particular match, the player attempts 10 shots. What is the probability that the player makes exactly 6 successful shots? Now, consider a different scenario where the player's success rate drops to 50% but the number of attempts remains the same. What is the probability of making exactly 6 successful shots in this scenario? Finally, consider a third scenario where the player's success rate remains at 50% but the number of attempts increases to 15. What is the probability of making exactly 6 successful shots in this third scenario?"

function.name: calc_binomial_prob
function.description: Calculates the probability of an outcome based on the binomial distribution Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

num_success.description: Number of times the event of interest has occurred.

prob_success.description: Probability of the event of interest on any single experiment. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Binomial set‑up**

For \(n\) independent trials with success probability \(p\),  
the probability of getting exactly \(k\) successes is  

\[
P(X=k)= \binom{n}{k}\,p^{\,k}(1-p)^{\,n-k}.
\]

Below we plug in the three sets of parameters.

---

### 1️⃣ \(n=10,\;p=0.60,\;k=6\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_1 &= \binom{10}{6}\,(0.6)^6\,(0.4)^4   \\[4pt]
    &= 210\times 0.046656 \times 0.0256     \\[4pt]
    &\approx 0.25082 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Result:** About **25.1 %** chance of exactly six made baskets.

---

### 2️⃣ \(n=10,\;p=0.50,\;k=6\)

Because \(p=\tfrac12\),

\[
P_2 = \binom{10}{6}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{10}
      = 210 \times \frac{1}{1024}
      \approx 0.20508 .
\]

> **Result:** Roughly **20.5 %** probability of six successes when shooting half the time.

---

### 3️⃣ \(n=15,\;p=0.50,\;k=6\)

Now there are more trials:

\[
\begin{aligned}
P_3 &= \binom{15}{6}\left(\tfrac12\right)^{15}\\[4pt]
    &= 5005 \times \frac{1}{32768}\\[4pt]
    &\approx 0.15283 .
\end{aligned}
\]

> **Result:** Approximately **15.3 %** chance of hitting exactly six out of fifteen shots.

---

#### Quick reference table

| Trials (\(n\)) | Success % (\(p\)) | Exactly 6 hits |
|-----------------|-------------------|----------------|
| 10              | 60 %              | 0.2508 (~25.1 %) |
| 10              | 50 %              | 0.2051 (~20.5 %) |
| 15              | 50 %              | 0.1528 (~15.3 %) |

These figures come directly from the binomial probability mass function.
